newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends lower, BOK sells dollars.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends lower, BOK sells dollars.

text.p: The won closed lower against the dollar on Friday despite the central bank's intervention as the prospects of dollar shortages propelled buying of the U.S. unit, dealers said.
The won closed at 897.50 after opening at 894.00. It touched 899.30, the lowest since the country introduced the market average system in March 1990.
The Bank of Korea sold dollars twice at 897.00 late in the morning and at 899.00 just before the close to support the won. The sales were estimated at $100 to $150 million, dealers said.
The won's mid-rate is expectd to be pegged at 896.50 on Monday, compared with 892.90 today.
Dealers said speculators were betting the central bank was losing its ability to brake the won's slide because of dwindling foreign currency holdings.
The Bank of Korea announced foreign exchange reserves of $30 billion at the end of February.
Dealers estimated the reserves were now down to about $25 billion after bouts of dollar selling and dollar supplies to banks.
Foreign exchange reserves of $35 billion are appropriate given the nation's monthly import bill of $11 billion, they said.
The won has been under pressure largely because of slumping exports.

The current account deficit rose to $2.45 billion in February from $1.97 billion a year before. The deficit for 1996 was $23.72 billion against $10.06 billion in 1995. It is officially forecast to be $18 billion this year.
Dealers forecast trading would range from 897.00 to 903.00 on Monday.
